content:
Last week, Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, accusing a former employee of stealing trade secrets "for OpenAI's benefit."

According to reports, during the lawsuit process, Apple has directly sent letters to dozens of former employees who now work at OpenAI.

According to the Financial Times, Apple has issued evidence preservation letters to approximately 40 former employees.

An evidence preservation letter is a formal written notice sent to an individual or organisation, requiring them to preserve documents, records and other evidence that may be related to a legal dispute. Such letters typically clearly specify what needs to be preserved.

This move stems from Apple's suspicion that the trade secret theft may not be limited to those named in last week's initial lawsuit.

To recap, Apple's lawsuit names OpenAI and io Products as defendants, along with former Apple employees Chang Liu and Tang Tan.

You can click here to learn more about the details of Apple's lawsuit against OpenAI:

  • Apple sues OpenAI, accusing former employees of stealing trade secrets
  • An erroneous email caused pre-lawsuit negotiations between Apple and OpenAI to derail
  • Apple lawsuit reveals the number of former employees currently working at OpenAI
  • OpenAI says it has seen no evidence to support Apple's allegations of trade secret theft
  • OpenAI's hardware timeline remains unchanged after Apple lawsuit
